operations.comment: ; PRG bank 0 (8 KiB, physical $00010-$0200F), mapped at $8000
; Sound driver bank (pair 0, mapped by InitSound/UpdateSoundSafe with SelectPrgPairNoSave).
; $8000 = SoundInit, $8034 = SoundUpdate (called once per NMI).  Four channel streams (pulse 1,
; pulse 2, triangle, noise; index SndChannel) are read from per-channel pointers; a sound effect
; owns channels through the SfxChannelMask bits and silences the music on them.  Data formats
; (note bytes below $20 are pitches into NotePeriodTable, values >= $20 set durations, negative
; bytes are commands handled at SndStreamCommand) are read from the code; the command set is
; only partly decoded. Also holds the palette sets used by LoadPalette16 and other data.
; Reset the sound driver: no music/effect requests, sweep units off, master level $7F, enable
; One frame of the driver.  A pending effect request is started at SndStartSfx; otherwise the
; four music channels are processed in turn (SndChannel 0-3): when a channel's timer expires its
; stream is read (notes, durations, commands), periods are written for channels not owned by an
; effect, then envelopes/vibrato are applied (SndApplyEnvelope, SndApplyVolume).  The effect
; Per-channel loop body (channel SndChannel): note whether an effect owns the channel, count down
; its note timer and read the stream when it expires; otherwise only the envelope step runs.
; Stream read ended on channel 3: leave through SndChannelsDone.
; Write the volume (unless the duty byte bit 7 is set) and continue with the next channel unless
; All four music channels done: reset SndChannel to 0 and run the effect sequencer (SndUpdateSfx).
; Handler addresses for stream commands $80-$8F (16 words, used as RTS targets after -1).
; Stream byte >= $80: driver command.  $FF ends the track (SfxRequestFlag = 0); otherwise
; command ($80-$8F) is dispatched by pushing SndCommandTable[cmd-$80]-1 and returning (RTS
; trick). Handlers: $80 volume/instrument, $81/$82 volume up/down, $83 set octave, $84/$85
; octave up/down, $86 default duration, $87 transpose, $88 duty, $89 counted jump, $8A jump,
; $8B/$8C loop start/end, $8D vibrato, $8E note cut, $8F loop break.
; Command $80 n: n < $10 = fixed volume n (low nibble of the duty/volume shadow $07E0,
; instrument $0425 cleared); n >= $10 selects volume envelope n-$10 from SndEnvelopeTable
; ($0441/$0442 = its first two bytes, $0417/$0418 = pointer to the steps).
; Command $81: raise the channel volume by one (SndChanDutyVol += 1).
; Command $82: lower the channel volume by one (SndChanDutyVol -= 1).
; Command $83 n: SndChanOctave = (n-1)*24 (12 notes x 2 bytes per octave in NotePeriodTable).
; Command $86 n: default note duration SndChanDuration = n.
; Command $87 n: SndChanTranspose = n (added to the period low byte).
; Command $88 n: duty bits 7-6 of the channel register shadow $07E0 = n bits 1-0.
; Command $89 k n lo hi: counted jump using counter k ($07EA+k).  A counter at $FF is loaded
; with n; it is decremented on every pass: while nonzero the jump bytes are skipped, when it
; reaches zero it is reset to $FF and the stream continues at lo/hi (SndCmdJump).  Gives "jump
; Command $8A lo hi: continue the stream at the given address.
; Command $8B n: push a loop (count n in $044C, return pointer in $045C) on the channel's
; Command $8C: decrement the innermost loop count; jump back to its start until it reaches 0,
; Command $8D rate [depth width delay]: rate 0 turns vibrato off (2 bytes); otherwise $043B =
; rate, $0438 = depth (period step), $0435 = width*2, $0432 = delay (5 bytes).
; Command $8E n: note length limit $07E4 = n (frames before the note is cut); n equal to the
; track tempo byte $07D9 disables the cut ($07E7 = $FF).
; Command $8F: drop the innermost loop level (SndLoopDepth -= 1) without jumping back.
; Per-channel note processing after the stream step (channel SndChannel): 1. note cut: $07E7
; counts down from $07E4 at the start of each note; at 0 the note becomes a rest. 2. volume
; envelope restart on a rest/new note ($0441/$0442 -> $041F/$0420 pointer). 3. volume envelope
; step: entries (volume, frames); a negative volume byte holds ($0428). 4. vibrato: after the
; delay $EC,X, every $043B frames the period low byte moves by $0438 up/down
;    between the limits set by $0435 ($EF,X counter, $F2,X direction), written to the APU unless
; Write channel X's duty/volume register (Y = 4*X) from the shadow $07E0.  MusicStatus is used
; as a fade-out level here: the volume is reduced by MusicStatus (minimum 1 or 2), the triangle
; is muted when the fade passes 5, and every $12-$18 frames (counter $0447, stepped on channel
; 2) the fade advances; at 10 the music stops (MusicStatus = $FF, SfxRequestFlag = 0).  Rests
; write volume 0 ($30/$80). Skipped for channels owned by a sound effect.
; Negative request slot: count it ($07D1) and rank it $7F.
; Sound-effect sequencer.  The five request slots MusicRequest..$07DF are ranked by the priority
; table SfxPriorityTable ($9D00, lower = more important, $7F = lowest); the best request becomes
; SndSfxState. It replaces the running effect when its priority is not worse than SfxPriority;
; it then loads the effect stream (SfxStreamPtrs $9D28) and takes over channels as its commands
; touch them.  Each frame the effect stream is interpreted: byte $FF ends the effect (channels
; returned to the music, priority reset to $7F); otherwise the high nibble selects channel+1
; ($FE) and the low nibble a command from SfxCommandTable: 0 volume, 1 period, 2 volume add, 3/5
; period up/down, 4 volume fade, 6 wait n frames, 7 wait add, 8/9 loop.
; SndSfxState: 0 = no effect, $FF = effect running (wait counter $0481), otherwise a new effect
; Handler addresses for effect commands 0-9 (words, RTS targets after -1).
; Word: effect stream restarted by SndSfxSpecial when MusicSpecial is requested.
; MusicSpecial request: restart the effect stream at the fixed pointer $86C2/$86C3.
; End of effect: give the channels back (SndLoadTrack), clear SndSfxState/SfxChannelMask,
; Dispatch one effect stream byte: values $0F and below are command numbers; larger bytes carry a
; count in the high nibble (stored minus one in $FE) and the command in the low nibble.  The
; command handler is entered through SfxCommandTable with the RTS trick (address - 1 pushed).
; Effect command 0 v: channel volume register value $047C = v.
; Effect command 1 lo hi: set the channel period ($07B8/$07B9) and write it to the APU.
; Effect command 2 n: SfxChanVolume += n (written by SfxCmdCommit).
; Effect command 3 n: period += n (written to the APU; high byte only on carry).
; Effect command 4 n: volume register value -= n, keeping the constant-volume bit $10.
; Effect command 6 n: wait n frames ($0480/$0481) before the next command.
; Effect command 7 n: SfxWaitReload += n and restart the wait with it (longer waits from now
; Effect command 8 n: push a loop (count $07C1, return pointer $07C6; depth $07C0).
; Effect command 9: repeat the innermost loop until its count is exhausted.
; Bit mask per channel ($01,$02,$04,$08) tested against SfxChannelMask.
; Common tail of commands 0-5: mark the channel as owned by the effect (SfxChannelMask) and
; Give effect-owned channels back to the music: for each pulse channel in SfxChannelMask restore
; the music's volume (or silence a resting channel) and period registers; silence the noise
; channel; then clear the request slots (MusicRequest..$07DF = $FF).  Name kept from round 1.
; Start music track SfxRequest: clear the channel work areas $0400-$0481 and $07B8-$07FD, read

; stream pointers (SndChanPtr), set $07E0-$07FD to $FF, and arm every channel timer to 1.
